summary: EfficientNet-B5 paired-view Phase 3 v2 visual-retention run using full images plus 456px crops, task_gated_residual fusion, crop_prior initialization, lr=5e-5, reduced backbone_lr_scale=0.05, batch_size=2, grad_accum_steps=12, cosine scheduler, and unfrozen Phase 1/2 heads. The run warm-started from outputs/data2/b5_pair_v2/phase2/best_model_phase2.pth and trained 14 tasks: the 7 existing Phase 1/2 tasks plus 7 visual/context Phase 3 fields. current_use and original_use were intentionally excluded via --phase3-labels after Phase 3 v1 showed they were weak image-only targets. Training requested 30 epochs and early-stopped after epoch 11 under patience 10. Best overall accuracy was 61.59% at epoch 10 across 14 tasks; best validation loss was 1.1318 at epoch 1. Compared with Phase 3 v1, v2 improves the overall Phase 3 result and slightly improves several visual fields while removing the two weakest use fields. It does not sufficiently restore Phase 1/2 retention versus the paired-v2 Phase 2 checkpoint, so use this as the best Phase 3 diagnostic run so far, not as the production replacement for Phase 1/2.

checkpoint_selection.checkpoint_epoch10.pth: Periodic checkpoint at epoch 10, which also matches the best-accuracy epoch.

results.trend: Training loss declined from 0.4443 at epoch 1 to 0.3062 by epoch 11. Validation loss was best immediately at epoch 1 and then rose, while overall accuracy improved from 60.97% at epoch 1 to 61.59% at epoch 10 before slipping slightly to 61.33% at epoch 11. This repeats the B5 pattern where validation loss is conservative and metric-based checkpointing is more useful than loss-only selection.

vs_phase3_full_v1.overall: +3.38 percentage_points by best accuracy (61.59% across 14 tasks vs 58.21% across 16 tasks). Some of this gain comes from excluding current_use and original_use, but v2 also improves several retained Phase 3 visual fields.
vs_phase3_full_v1.old_task_retention: Mixed. Stories improved substantially versus v1 (+3.89pp at best-accuracy checkpoints), roof_type and building_form were essentially flat, chimney_present improved, while primary_cladding and setting remained weak and architectural_style was slightly lower.
vs_phase3_full_v1.landscape_features: -0.72pp Jaccard at best-accuracy checkpoints (39.56% vs 40.28%), though v2's per-task best reached 40.93%.
vs_phase3_full_v1.entrance: -0.36pp Jaccard at best-accuracy checkpoints (40.49% vs 40.85%), but macro F1 improved to 41.09% at epoch 10.
vs_phase3_full_v1.associated_buildings: +0.60pp Jaccard at best-accuracy checkpoints (31.31% vs 30.71%) and macro F1 improved to 23.69%.
vs_phase3_full_v1.building_category: +0.13pp accuracy at best-accuracy checkpoints (95.01% vs 94.88%), roughly tied.
vs_phase3_full_v1.roof_materials: Slightly lower Jaccard at best-accuracy checkpoints (90.38% vs 90.76%), essentially tied and still dominated by common labels.

vs_b5_pair_v2_phase2_best_accuracy.overall: Not directly comparable as a single headline because v2 overall averages 14 tasks while Phase 2 averaged 7 tasks. V2 best overall was 61.59%; Phase 2 best overall was 76.22%.
vs_b5_pair_v2_phase2_best_accuracy.stories: -6.99pp (66.63% vs 73.62%). This is better than v1's -10.88pp but still not retained enough.
vs_b5_pair_v2_phase2_best_accuracy.roof_type: -5.79pp (56.31% vs 62.10%). Essentially unchanged from v1's roof retention problem.
vs_b5_pair_v2_phase2_best_accuracy.primary_cladding: -14.06pp (63.64% vs 77.70%) at the best-overall checkpoint. Even its per-task best accuracy of 65.79% remains far below Phase 2.
vs_b5_pair_v2_phase2_best_accuracy.setting_exact: -9.99pp (64.79% vs 74.78%). Setting remains under-retained despite full-heavy routing.

comparison.interpretation: Excluding current_use and original_use and slowing the backbone to 0.05 improved the Phase 3 visual-retention run versus v1, but it did not solve retention. The remaining retention loss is likely caused by the added visual heads and shared representation drift, not just the weak use fields.

learnings: The --phase3-labels visual subset works end-to-end and is the right default for the next Phase 3 visual experiments. current_use and original_use should remain out of the shared visual-retention run for now.

Reducing backbone_lr_scale from 0.1 to 0.05 plus removing use fields improved overall Phase 3 behavior, especially stories retention and several visual fields, but the old-task regression is still too large for production replacement.

Primary_cladding is the biggest unresolved retention failure. V2 primary_cladding at best overall is 63.64%, worse than v1's 65.58% and far below paired-v2 Phase 2 at 77.70%. This task may need either higher old-task weighting, a task-specific route, or less backbone movement.
Stories improved versus v1, supporting the crop-preserving strategy, but still lags the Phase 2 checkpoint by about 7pp.
Setting remains weak in Phase 3 despite full-heavy defaults. This suggests the shared multitask update, not just gate initialization, is degrading the setting representation.
Visual Phase 3 fields are learnable and fairly consistent: window, entrance, wall_features, landscape_features, roof_materials, and building_category all show repeatable signal across v1 and v2.

Best loss and best accuracy diverged again. The best-loss checkpoint is epoch 1, while the best-accuracy checkpoint is epoch 10. Continue selecting comparison checkpoints by the target metric, not validation loss alone.
next_steps: Keep outputs/data2/b5_pair_v2/phase2/best_model_phase2.pth as the production/comparison checkpoint for Phase 1/2.
Use outputs/data2/phase3_v2_visual_retention/phase3/best_model_phase3.pth as the best Phase 3 visual diagnostic checkpoint so far, but not as the production replacement.

Run Phase 3 v3 with stronger old-task protection: either lower backbone_lr_scale to 0.01-0.02, freeze the backbone for a short head-adaptation stage, or add explicit old-task loss upweighting for primary_cladding, stories, roof_type, and setting.

Consider reducing the Phase 3 visual loss weights another 25-50% if the goal is strict Phase 1/2 retention. V2 removed weak use fields but retained visual Phase 3 pressure is still enough to move old representations.

Prioritize a per-label report for window, entrance, wall_features, landscape_features, associated_buildings, and roof_materials before tuning those heads further. Aggregate Jaccard is not enough to identify which labels are truly learned.
Keep current_use and original_use as separate experiments after the visual-retention path is stable, ideally with more data or metadata/context features.
operational_notes: The run completed with exit code 0 and early-stopped after epoch 11 under early_stopping_patience=10.
The output directory contains best_model_phase3.pth, best_model_by_loss_phase3.pth, checkpoint_epoch10.pth, run_config.json, training_history.json, and this run_notes.json.

The saved run_config.json records phase3_labels as wall_features,landscape_features,window,entrance,associated_buildings,building_category,roof_materials. current_use and original_use were not trained in this run.

The saved run_config.json records git_commit 632eabd, which predates some uncommitted Phase 3 implementation changes in the working tree. Interpret this commit field as the repository HEAD at run start, not a clean committed provenance marker.
Large .pth files remain ignored by git. Only run_config.json, training_history.json, and run_notes.json should be considered for lightweight run documentation if committing outputs.
